correctness.rationale: The exact tensor-product projector decomposition gives all four matrix-entry orbits for every integer \(n\ge2\). Direct common-denominator expansion proves the critical entries equal \(12hA_n/(D(2h)D(nh)D((n+2)h))\) and similarly with \(B_n\); the diagonal and opposite-coordinate entries are always positive. Descartes signs classify the \(B_n\)-root and bound \(A_n\) to two positive roots. Exact Sturm endpoint sign patterns exhaust \(n=7,\ldots,17\); an explicit \(8/n\) negative witness and a positive \(\sqrt{12/n}\) recovery witness prove and order both roots for every \(n\ge18\). The actual included checker executed successfully with 255 exact symbolic/rational checks and exact full matrices for sizes 2 through 6. No finite experiment substitutes for the universal argument.

originality.rationale: Direct examination of the relevant full published OA analyses and mathematical records found no result determining two positive-length nonnegative-step intervals for reversible diffusion on the entire \(K_2\square K_n\) family or the sharp integer onset at \(n=18\). The previously established [2/2] Padé loss of positivity, zero absolute-monotonicity radius, and eight-state directed-birth example do not imply this graph-specific phase diagram. Only best-knowledge originality is claimed; inaccessible or unindexed equivalent coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: Unindexed or less accessible numerical diffusion studies could contain an equivalent family-specific theorem.

value.rationale: Nonnegativity of a diffusion time step is a fundamental qualitative feature not guaranteed by A-stability. The finding classifies all admissible steps on a natural infinite reversible family, identifies an exact finite-size onset at 36 states, and proves a genuinely disconnected positive-step set: an intermediate invalid step can be followed by a later valid step. These facts directly affect assumptions behind monotone step-size selection and cannot be obtained merely by applying a textbook timestep bound.
